payload.description:
As an evaluation owner, I want closed-world scope to live on reviewed packet-and-layer metadata, so that a layer reviewed exhaustively with zero positives can still catch hallucinated findings, and so that scope is not duplicated across 434 positive annotations.

Out of scope: detector retuning; changing which files ingest can open; publishing a baseline.

```gherkin
Feature: Closed-world scope lives on packet-and-layer metadata

Scenario: A reviewed layer with no positives still measures false positives
  Given a packet layer that was reviewed exhaustively and has no accepted positives
  When the scanner emits a finding in a reviewed file that was successfully processed
  Then the finding is scored as a false positive

Scenario: Scope is not repeated on every positive annotation
  Given a packet layer with reviewed file scope
  When gold is loaded
  Then scope comes from packet-and-layer metadata
  And positive annotations do not each carry exhaustive_scope_files

Scenario: Precision uses reviewed files that were successfully processed
  Given reviewed scope that includes files ingest cannot open
  When precision is computed
  Then unread files are not in the precision denominator
```
payload.title: Closed-world scope lives on packet-and-layer metadata
